data.narrative:
Ricursive Intelligence is a Series A-stage semiconductor company founded by Anna Goldie and Azalia Mirhoseini that has raised $335M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a peer universe of 3 same-stage private companies in chips and semiconductors (SambaNova Systems at $11.0B, Rebellions at $2.3B, and d-Matrix at $2.0B), supplemented by public comparables including NVIDIA, AMD, and Anduril Labs trading at a median 20.5x price-to-sales.

Two valuation methods proved applicable. Stage-progression analysis, using total raised as a proxy base and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A advancement, yields $670M. Peer-median anchoring across the three same-sector, same-stage private comparables produces $2.3B, though the range spans $2.0B to $11.0B, reflecting material dispersion. Public-comp anchoring via price-to-sales multiples cannot be applied without disclosed revenue figures, which remain private.

Triangulating these two methods yields a valuation range of $570M (low) to $2.7B (high), with a median of $1.5B. The wide range reflects meaningful uncertainty around growth trajectory and capital intensity relative to peers. The stage-progression floor appears conservative relative to peer medians; the peer-median anchored estimate likely represents the most defensible midpoint given comparable-stage positioning. Revenue disclosure and closer technical assessment of competitive positioning would narrow this range materially.
